findings.message: A failed return overwrites the record of a return that already succeeded. `recordReturn` updates `result` on the state row whenever the hash and user match, even when `storeConnect` has already set `result = 'connected'` on that row. Two returns that carry the same state share one row and one `ref`, so the last writer decides what both screens say. The new result-112 test case "a link already used" relies on this overwrite. Fix: let only the first outcome stand (add `and result is null` to the update, and return the id whatever the update did), or record each return on its own row and send that row's id as `ref`. Add a test that runs two real callbacks with the same state.
findings.scenario: The person clicks the chat card's "Continue to GitHub" link twice. GitHub has already authorised the app, so it redirects both tabs at once with the same state. Tab A connects and writes result='connected'. Tab B's claim fails with 'expired', and its recordReturn sets result='expired' on the same row. Tab A reloads /git-accounts?github=1&ref=<id> and shows the red "that link has expired or was already used" next to the "Connected as @kasun-dias" card.

findings.message: When the result can't be recorded or read, the screen tells the person GitHub wasn't connected. On a successful connect, the callback runs a second audited service (`recordReturn`) only to look up the row id again by state hash. If that call fails, the `.catch` logs it and returns `{ id: null }`, and ResultNote then shows UNMATCHED ("GitHub wasn't connected. Ask amax to connect GitHub again."), even though `storeConnect` committed the connection. The extra service is also unneeded (B11): it writes an audit row for what is only a select, and `completeConnect` already has `claimId`. Fix: return `claimId` from `completeConnect` and use it as `ref` on success. Delete the `connected` select branch of `recordReturn`. When the result can't be recorded, show a neutral 'couldn't read the result' note, never a negative claim.
findings.scenario: completeConnect succeeds, then recordReturn throws (connection reset or pool timeout). The query is {github:'1'} with no ref, so the screen shows "GitHub wasn't connected. Ask amax to connect GitHub again." while the identities are stored. The person reconnects for nothing.

findings.message: `recordReturn` accepts any string as `result` (`z.string()`) and writes it to `connect_state.result`. Validate it against the ResultCode list (`z.enum(Object.keys(RESULTS))`), so that only codes the screen knows are ever stored.

After the 10-minute window, a reload of the person's own successful return shows the red UNMATCHED sentence ("GitHub wasn't connected") beside the Connected card. The two say opposite things. When the person is connected, show nothing in place of the negative sentence (AC-2 allows 'or nothing').
findings.scenario: The person connects, leaves the tab, and reloads /git-accounts?github=1&ref=<id> 15 minutes later. The red "GitHub wasn't connected" note appears above "GitHub · Connected as @kasun-dias".

findings.message: The signed-out e2e uses a made-up state, so it only shows that the redirect chain ends on UNMATCHED. It never shows that a real return, interrupted by sign-in, finishes the connect after resume. A broken resume (a lost or double-encoded query) would still pass. Drive a real state: issue the connect, sign out, hit the callback with that state and code=good, sign in, and expect 'GitHub connected'.
findings.scenario: ResumeReturn double-encodes the query, so `state` arrives mangled. The connect fails with 'incomplete', and the test still passes because it expects UNMATCHED.
